change.title: API 2026-10 became current/default on 2026-10-26; 2026-07 moves to maintenance; 2027-01 is RC, current 2027-01-15

source.quote: If you don't, your app will always get the Current version.

tasks.reasoning: monday's versioning doc says apps that don't send an API-Version header always get the Current version. This repo sends none. So the 2026-10 switch already changed the schema it runs against, and on 2027-01-15 it will move to 2027-01 with no code change. The repo's queries use items_by_column_values and boards.items. To my knowledge both were removed in monday's 2023-10 API in favor of items_page_by_column_values and boards.items_page. If so, these calls may already be failing under the current default. That removal is not among the listed changes, so this is uncertain. The migration agent should: (1) add an explicit API-Version header (e.g. 2026-10) to the got.extend client; (2) run each query against that version, rewriting items_by_column_values and boards.items to items_page_by_column_values and items_page if they are rejected; (3) confirm change_multiple_column_values and create_item still validate.

callSites.why: run() POSTs every GraphQL query (items_by_column_values, boards.items, change_multiple_column_values, create_item) to /v2. The usage map shows no API-Version header, so each request is served by whatever version is Current: 2026-10 since 2026-10-26, and 2027-01 from 2027-01-15.
The got.extend client sets only the authorization header. This is where an explicit API-Version header should be added to stop the version from floating.

## API 2026-10 became current/default on 2026-10-26; 2026-07 moves to maintenance; 2027-01 is RC, current 2027-01-15 [Verified]

### Change

src/api/monday.js now sends API-Version: 2026-10. find and findAll use items_page_by_column_values, boards.items_page and next_items_page, and follow the cursor when no limit is given. The save mutation declares $bId as ID!. Added test/monday.test.js, which mocks got.

Files touched:
- `src/api/monday.js`
- `test/monday.test.js`

### Why

The client sent no version header, so it always ran against monday's Current version (2026-10 now, 2027-01 on 2027-01-15). The old items_by_column_values and boards.items fields and Int board ids are not in the 2026-10 schema.

> If you don't, your app will always get the Current version.

Source: https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/docs/api-versioning

Test of this change: `monday-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Argument types of change_multiple_column_values and create_item are assumed (board_id: ID, column_values: JSON). The static check passed, but I did not read their argument lists.
- Pinned 2026-10 only; behaviour at 2027-01 is untested.
- Response shape of column_values text was not checked.
- The test mocks got, so it cannot catch runtime errors from the real API.

### Behaviour changes

- Requests now pin API-Version 2026-10 instead of floating on Current. The pin needs a manual bump later.
- find with no limit now returns all matches by paging 500 at a time via the cursor. The old query returned every match in one call.
- findAll with no limit pages through the whole board via next_items_page.
- A limit passed to find or findAll now caps the result at one page, with no cursor following.
- Board id variables are typed ID! instead of Int!.

review.summary: The diff targets the right problem. With no API-Version header, the app always got the Current version, and on 2026-10 the old `items_by_column_values`, `boards { items }` and `Int` board IDs no longer exist. The rewrite to `items_page_by_column_values`, `items_page`/`next_items_page` and `ID!` covers all three exports in src/api/monday.js (find, findAll, save). The diff also goes beyond the forced change: it pins the version, adds automatic full pagination and changes the semantics of `limit`. The only check is a new, fully mocked test, so nothing confirms the queries against the real 2026-10 schema. The 'verified' grade overstates what that mocked test proves.

concerns.issue: Lines 4-10 add `'API-Version': '2026-10'`, which pins the app instead of following Current. That is defensible, but it is a policy change. The old `items(limit:)` accepted larger values; items_page caps `limit` (500 as far as I know, unconfirmed for 2026-10). A caller passing limit > 500 will now get an error, and even if accepted it would only get one page, because pagination is disabled whenever `limit` is set.

With limit=0, find and findAll used to issue a single request and take the API's default result. They now page through the whole board 500 items at a time. For large boards that means more requests and more complexity-budget usage, and cursors expire after about 60 minutes. This may be the intended behaviour, but it is a change.

I could not confirm from the quoted source (a versioning page) the exact 2026-10 signatures: `ItemsPageByColumnValuesQuery!` with `column_id` and `column_values`, `next_items_page(cursor: String!, limit:)`, `boards(ids: [ID!])` taking a scalar `bId` through list coercion, and `column_values(ids: [String])` still exposing `text`. Check these against the 2026-10 schema or API playground.

The test mocks `got` and keys responses on query substrings, so it never validates the GraphQL against a schema. It does not cover multi-page `find`, the `limit` path, `save` with create_item, or error handling. The assertion `assert(!/.../.test(''))` is a no-op. The 'before fail' result is trivial, since the test is new and asserts the newly added header.

The grade is 'verified', but the only evidence is this mocked test, written alongside a substantial query rewrite. 'needs-review' would match the evidence better until the queries have run against a real 2026-10 board.

change.title: npm got 16.0.0: new built-in HTTP/2 client, drops http2-wrapper and cacheable-lookup, strips credentials on cross-origin redirects

source.quote: Rewrite HTTP/2 support and drop the `http2-wrapper` dependency (#2464) 1e157c4

tasks.reasoning:
The lockfile pins got 11.8.2, five majors behind. Nothing breaks today; these changes bite only when the dependency is bumped. They are handled together as one upgrade to got 16 so a single PR covers everything the bump breaks: convert require('got') to ESM import (or dynamic import), raise the Node runtime to 22, and replace any promise.cancel()/isStream use. Also verify credentials are still sent, since got 16 strips credentials on cross-origin redirects. The monday authorization header and the Google API key in the query string are both affected if redirects occur. got is used by all three usages (monday, google-translate, recipepuppy). The migration agent should confirm each file imports got from the shared package-lock.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- monday:got-12-0-0 (sdk-major): npm got 12.0.0: pure ESM, requires Node 14, effective 2021-12-10. The repo pins got 11.8.2. Moving to got 16 crosses 12.0.0, so the code must switch to ESM import (got is pure ESM) and Node >=14 within the same PR.
  Source: https://api.github.com/repos/sindresorhus/got/releases?per_page=100
  "### This package is now pure ESM"
- monday:got-13-0-0 (sdk-major): npm got 13.0.0: requires Node 16, enableUnixSockets defaults to false, effective 2023-05-27. Crossed by the same upgrade. Raises Node to 16 and makes enableUnixSockets false by default; the repo calls HTTPS hosts only, so this is just a check.
  Source: https://api.github.com/repos/sindresorhus/got/releases?per_page=100
  "Change the [`enableUnixSockets`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/blob/main/documentation/2-options.md#enableunixsockets) option to be `false` by default 852c312"
- monday:got-14-0-0 (sdk-major): npm got 14.0.0: requires Node.js 20, effective 2023-11-29. Crossed by the same upgrade. Requires Node.js 20, handled in the runtime bump of this PR.
  Source: https://api.github.com/repos/sindresorhus/got/releases?per_page=100
  "Require Node.js 20 (#2313) a004263"
- monday:got-15-0-0 (sdk-major): npm got 15.0.0: requires Node 22, removes promise.cancel() and isStream, strictContentLength default true, effective 2026-04-01. Crossed by the same upgrade. Requires Node 22, removes promise.cancel() and isStream, and defaults strictContentLength to true; all checked in this one PR.
  Source: https://api.github.com/repos/sindresorhus/got/releases?per_page=100
  "`promise.cancel()` is gone. Use the [`signal` option](https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/blob/main/documentation/2-options.md#signal) with [`AbortController`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/AbortController) instead."

callSites.why: Builds the client with got.extend and a headers option. After the upgrade it needs an ESM import and must still extend correctly.
run() POSTs JSON with got and reads the response body and errors. The response and error API changed across majors 12–16.
POSTs to Google Translate with got and reads data.translations[0].translatedText. Needs the ESM import and a check of the response and error handling.
GET with got that reads body.results. Needs the ESM import and a check of the JSON response handling.
GET with got that reads body.results.length. Same got upgrade impact.

record.prBody:
## npm got 16.0.0: new built-in HTTP/2 client, drops http2-wrapper and cacheable-lookup, strips credentials on cross-origin redirects [Needs review]

### Change

Upgraded got 11.8.2 to 16.2.0 with npm 6. Replaced require('got') in monday.js, translate.js and recipe.js with a lazily created client via dynamic import('got'), since got is pure ESM and the app is CommonJS. Set engines.node to >=22 and moved the Dockerfile base image from alpine-node 12 to node:22-alpine. Added test/got.test.js, registered as the check "got16".

Files touched:
- `Dockerfile`
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `src/api/monday.js`
- `src/api/recipe.js`
- `src/api/translate.js`
- `test/got.test.js`

### Why

got 12 made the package pure ESM, and got 15 and 16 need Node 22, so require('got') and the Node 12 image both break. The repo does not use promise.cancel(), isStream, unix sockets, HTTP/2 or content-length, so those changes need no code change.

> Rewrite HTTP/2 support and drop the `http2-wrapper` dependency (#2464) 1e157c4

Source: https://api.github.com/repos/sindresorhus/got/releases?per_page=100

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| got16 | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- got16, added by the agent: `node test/got.test.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No live calls were made. The mocked test only checks the got version, that the modules load, and that got.extend exists. It does not exercise the requests.
- Credential stripping on cross-origin redirects was not tested. The monday API and Google Translate do not normally redirect, and recipepuppy is plain http and may redirect. Its calls send no credentials.
- The monday GraphQL queries are untouched. They use the old items_by_column_values and boards.items shapes and Int board ids, and they are probably already broken on the current monday API version. That is a separate migration, and I did not run graphql_check.
- The Docker image build was not run.
- The agent wrote no test of this change and gave no reason why none can be written.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The got client is now created on the first request instead of at module load.
- The runtime must be Node 22 or later. The Dockerfile base image changed from alpine-node 12 to node:22-alpine.
- The got 16 defaults now apply: strictContentLength, enableUnixSockets off, and credentials stripped on cross-origin redirects.

---
